summary: We are testing whether adding or-opt1 (single-city relocation using KNN candidate lists) to the existing 2-opt + ILS local search pipeline improves the penalized TSP tour score beyond the ~78.93 baseline established in iteration 2. Two arms will run: a treatment arm with or-opt1 integrated into the search loop, and a negative control rerunning the v25 baseline.
key_points: Treatment arm adds a new move type (or-opt1: remove a city and reinsert it near a KNN neighbor) that explores a neighborhood 2-opt cannot reach — specifically, relocating a single city without reversing the intervening segment. It also adds dist² early rejection to speed up 2-opt.
Control arm reruns the validated v25 solution (2-opt + ILS only, no or-opt) expecting ~78.93 score, providing a direct comparison point and checking for environmental variability.

Confirmation criterion: treatment score exceeds control by ≥0.04 points consistently. Refutation: no improvement or regression, which would suggest either (a) or-opt1 finds zero improving moves on 2-opt-optimal tours, or (b) the time spent on or-opt1 steals budget from more productive 2-opt passes.
Key risk mitigated: or-opt2/3 (pair/triple relocation) were excluded due to TLE on large N from O(N) array shifts; only seg=1 with memmove is included, keeping within the 2-second time limit.
Time budget allocation: 50% for initial 2-opt, 8% for or-opt1, 7% for 2-opt redo, 10% for window 2-opt, remainder for ILS perturbation+recovery — all within 1900ms wall clock.
